**NEW Divine Judgment simultaneous-target order:** use printed source target order; otherwise declared target/list order fixed before damage, or stable area target application order established before resolving. First recipient taking positive damage supplies reflection magnitude; never sum victims. The turn entitlement is then spent.

Corpses, intrinsic class progression, Monk hard-denial history and Mirrorsage/Wizard archive-retention markers are bookkeeping rather than creature Marked. Existing Crimson Blood Mark, Oracle Mark of the Doomed, Paladin Grief and Warrior Vulnerable identities retain their reviewed rules.

preparedExcerpts.heading: Compulsion, action denial and initiative
preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## Compulsion, action denial and initiative

Keep Charmed/Frightened, one commanded Action, Reaction denial, Speed0/half and attack restrictions as distinct components. The shared source-character/target/encounter hard-denial guard controls new hard components across feature names. A used allowance blocks only a new hard component; apply an expressly printed soft fallback, otherwise do not invent one. Hard-control immunity and source restrictions still apply.

Oracle Bone Whisper, Ledger's Command, Marquis's Glimpse, Slumber Glimpse and Moment's Pause soft fallback records, and Paladin Decree/Echo of Ages soft fallbacks, carry slowed-foe eligibility only while their actual Speed component is active. Spiral Opens instead has a distinct player-Speed0 component; choosing a repeated action or using NPC Forced Echo does not gain that tag. Passive Stars Revelation Mastery is a HOOK authorizing a later enhanced Guiding Bolt component, not an immediate applied slow. The registry separates application, modifier and reader/bookkeeping references.

Ledger's Command may command one hostile Action under that guard; subsequent qualifying failures use its Reaction+Speed0 fallback. Bone Whisper, Marquis's Glimpse, Slumber Glimpse and Moment's Pause retain their own hard/fallback splits. Slumber's -2 initiative rider affects the next eligible initiative roll/check before encounter end, never an already-established slot. Its attack bonus is independently consumed.

Wizard Mental Binding/Arcane Domination and Paladin Decree of Submission retain only their printed first commanded turn; ongoing Charmed/Reaction/Speed riders cannot command another Action. Mind Prison's first Incapacitated/commanded replacement is separate from later half-Speed/no-Reaction riders. The player retains printed target/route choices and prohibitions on self-harm, beliefs, resource expenditure and permanent allegiance. An NPC Forced Echo from The Spiral Opens spends the hard-denial allowance and has no invented NPC fallback after it is used. Its player branch stays distinct. Royal Decree's target-chosen Prone-or-safe-movement retains Action/target choice and does not spend the whole-Action denial allowance.

Echo of Ages' attack denial uses the shared hard guard; later actual qualifying failed applications use its printed soft fallback. It does not gain a repeat trigger every round from concentration. Reign of Ashes is soft half-Speed/noDash/**no willing teleport benefit**, ending target-next-end. **NEW:** target cannot self-teleport or consent to another's transport; independently legal involuntary hostile displacement can still affect it unless that effect needs willingness. No Root/Restrained or universal planar anchoring is added.

**NEW Moment's Pause delay:** snapshot canonical initiative order excluding temporary delays. One pending delay per target per next numbered round; repeated applications do not stack. At next-round construction process stable application order. Find the first still-participating snapshot creature after the target, skipping removed/dead and ignoring new entrants absent from that snapshot; move target immediately after it. With no surviving later snapshot member leave current position. Chained delays are deterministic in application order; no participant is duplicated/deleted and no virtual duration/falling/recovery marker changes. The next following round resumes canonical order. This is distinct from modifying an initiative roll.

preparedExcerpts.heading: Root, physical restraints and suppression
preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## Root, physical restraints and suppression

Root supplies Speed0 only; it does not inherently apply Restrained, Grappled, Incapacitated, Action/Reaction loss or a teleport ban. A Speed0 source not named Root receives no invented Root identity. Multiple zero records coexist; ending one does not end another.

Printed restraint saves, escape Actions, size/anatomy limits, concentration and relationship endpoints win. **NEW fallback only** for genuine physical Restrained with no explicit escape, no sufficient fixed endpoint and no special-cure requirement: Action STR(Athletics) or DEX(Acrobatics) against recorded applying DC, otherwise10, ends **one selected** record on success. An adjacent helper may instead use Action STR(Athletics). None of the supplied active restraints needs this fallback. A fixed endpoint alone excludes it. No generic cutting, helper or object-HP escape is added to magical-only restraints.

Net Bolt retains printed Action STR(Athletics) escape, net AC10/HP5, maximum3 rounds and Huge+ -10 replacement. Tinker Net Trap retains its printed repeat save/Action escape. Earthen Grip's grounded-target requirement is an application requirement; the source does not say moving/teleporting away ends it. It persists after a legal teleport until concentration, printed time or its Action escape ends it. Tyrant's Impale and Panther retain their explicit reach/separation/reversion relationship endings. If suppression permits escape beyond a required maintained reach, the source ends and cannot resume. An attached physical net otherwise persists through suppression and can resume until removed/destroyed/expired.

Immunity suppresses only covered components; clocks and relationship checks continue. Word of Binding's Silenced and Speed0 are independent for immunity, while its successful repeat save ends both. A suppressed record does not grant active eligibility hooks. Ending one restriction does not cure unrelated damage, marks or components on the same card.

DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/me.fullCurrentText: # Conditions — integrated playtest reference **Status:** reviewed and reference-validated within generic Core condition/recovery scope. All28 Core condition identities preserved. New generic procedures are explicit playtest proposals, not edits to approved books or a claim of game-wide balance. [Core resolution and Wounds](CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md) · [Recovery and exposure procedures](CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md) · [Custom rider bindings](CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md) · [Development coverage](GAME_DEVELOPMENT_COVERAGE.md) The Core catalog contains all 28 conditions. The older shared class reference listed 15 of them; that was a reference omission, not lost source data. This overlay supplies the complete reference without modifying the books or that preserved class file. ## Shared handling This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications. Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. A generic cure naming a condition clears its source records unless a reviewed procedure specifies one-record scope. Bleeding Medicine and Burning DEX saves use the specific procedures below. Track Charmed, Frightened, Marked and Grappled relationships separately. Exhaustion, Intoxication, Unity and Wounds use their explicit tracks. Immunity to a named condition prevents that condition, including an inherited component, but does not silently grant immunity to every parent condition that can cause it. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration. Advantages and disadvantages never multiply dice: any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to one normal d20 roll, regardless of the number of sources. Automatic failure of a required check/save is resolved without a roll. A condition does not give a save where its source grants none. A critical-if-hit rider never makes a missed attack hit. Automatic failure has no rolled total: use ordinary Failure, not Critical Failure or an invented failure margin, unless the source explicitly supplies one. Generic Core Bleeding and Burning join family.bleeding and family.ongoing-fire respectively, with source-owner stack groups. At one identical target timing marker, all due generic and custom groups in that family compete: highest expected unmitigated damage, then earliest application. Only the winning group's source-permitted instances deal damage. All due groups consume that tick; losers do not defer or bank it. Different printed markers resolve separately. No record also receives a duplicate generic tick. Core generic timing is end of regular target turn; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative preserve one periodic step per complete six seconds with no duplicate interval across initiative transitions. Strain is not globally unique: expedition.strain and warrior.serum-strain are separate source-qualified tracks, both distinct from the six-level Exhaustion condition. See the Strain namespace reference for the current candidate. Oracle one-turn Revelation backlash is also separate from global Exhaustion; its printed penalties and endpoint remain unchanged. Wound Eater feeding failures explicitly use global Exhaustion. Never silently convert similarly named tracks. See CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md for finite recovery, cleansing, substance, Intoxication and Unity procedures. These new proposals are labeled separately from recovered source rules. Conditions do not reveal Director secrets or force player beliefs or decisions. SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. ## Quick index | Condition | Configuration | |---|---| | [Addicted](#addicted) | active provisional overlay | | [Bleeding](#bleeding) | active provisional overlay | | [Blinded](#blinded) | active provisional overlay | | [Burning](#burning) | active provisional overlay | | [Charmed](#charmed) | active provisional overlay | | [Corrupted](#corrupted) | active provisional overlay | | [Dazed](#dazed) | active provisional overlay | | [Deafened](#deafened) | active provisional overlay | | [Exhausted](#exhausted) | active provisional overlay | | [Frightened](#frightened) | active provisional overlay | | [Grappled](#grappled) | active provisional overlay | | [Incapacitated](#incapacitated) | active provisional overlay | | [Intoxicated](#intoxicated) | active provisional overlay | | [Invisible](#invisible) | active provisional overlay | | [Marked](#marked) | active provisional overlay | | [Paralyzed](#paralyzed) | active provisional overlay | | [Petrified](#petrified) | active provisional overlay | | [Poisoned](#poisoned) | active provisional overlay | | [Prone](#prone) | active provisional overlay | | [Resonance Burn](#resonance-burn) | preserved; inactive in this Dissonance configuration | | [Restrained](#restrained) | active provisional overlay | | [Silenced](#silenced) | active provisional overlay | | [Staggered](#staggered) | active provisional overlay | | [Stunned](#stunned) | active provisional overlay | | [Unconscious](#unconscious) | active provisional overlay | | [Unity Exposure](#unity-exposure) | active provisional overlay | | [Withdrawal](#withdrawal) | active provisional overlay | | [Wounded](#wounded) | active provisional overlay | ## Addicted **Preserved Core text:** The creature has dependence on a named substance. Without a maintenance dose after a long rest, it gains Withdrawal. **Effect:** Record dependence on one named substance. After each completed long rest, if the creature has not taken the required maintenance dose for that substance, apply Withdrawal for that substance. Existing source procedures for repeated doses, dependence DC, tolerance and overdose continue to operate. **Application:** Applied only by a substance or dependence procedure that explicitly creates or advances dependence. Merely consuming a substance does not automatically grant Addicted unless its procedure says so. **Duration and ending:** A new maintenance dose is due immediately after each completed long rest. Until taken, apply that substance's Withdrawal; a pre-rest dose cannot satisfy this new interval. A dose suppresses symptoms until the next maintenance interval, but dependence persists. A seven-day no-dose recovery project or an explicit dependence-removal effect can remove it; see CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md. **Stacking:** Track one Addicted record per named substance. Separate substance dependencies coexist; duplicate dependence on the same substance does not create multiple copies unless a source defines severity. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A feature explicitly preventing dependence blocks application. Magic that only removes symptoms does not automatically remove dependence, consistent with the source treatment text. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: maintenance dose may relieve that substance's current Withdrawal symptoms without removing Addicted; exact dependence cure procedure remains deferred. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Audit individual substance cards, dose escalation wording, equipment availability and specific cure effects during item integration. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 727, definition paragraph 728; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Bleeding **Preserved Core text:** Take damage equal to proficiency bonus at the end of each turn. An action and Medicine check or magical healing ends it. **Effect:** At the end of the affected creature's regular turn, take damage equal to its current PB, unless the selected reviewed application prints a different magnitude. Use that application's specified physical type; if none, slashing. **Application:** Only explicit Bleeding applications create a source record. Record DC (or 10), magnitude, type and endpoint. **Duration and ending:** Persists until its source or applicable cure ends it. Self or adjacent helper spends an Action selecting one active eligible Bleed record before a WIS (Medicine) check: printed cure DC, otherwise recorded applying effect/class/spell DC, otherwise 10. Success or Critical Success ends that record only. One legal magical healing event with positive pre-cap/pre-prohibition potential ends all ordinary records with an automatic-healing endpoint, even at full HP or while Corrupted/Decay prevents actual HP gain. Each Shaman Blood Curse instead gets its own printed CON save. Explicit end-one/end-all removers retain exact scope and protected-source exceptions. **Stacking:** Independent source-owner records enter unified family arbitration at their actual marker. No DC tie-break or separate generic damage layer. Medicine ends one selected record; positive-potential magical healing ends all eligible automatic-cure records. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Creatures explicitly immune to bleeding/blood-loss effects cannot gain it. Specific spell/class/item Bleeding numbers replace the generic PB magnitude only when printed. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: affected-creature PB; explicit physical type or slashing fallback; source DC or 10; one regular-turn tick and strongest-record selection. - Source-faithful clarification: magical healing need not increase current HP to end Bleeding. - SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 729, definition paragraph 730; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Blinded **Preserved Core text:** Cannot see; automatically fails sight checks; attacks have disadvantage and attacks against it have advantage. **Effect:** The creature cannot see, automatically fails checks that require sight, has disadvantage on attack rolls, and attack rolls against it have advantage. **Application:** Only an effect that explicitly inflicts Blinded applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save, cure or endpoint. **Stacking:** Multiple Blinded applications do not increase the penalties; track independent durations only when needed to know when all sources have ended. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A sense that does not require sight may still function. A feature explicitly allowing sight while Blinded overrides only its printed scope. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot see, automatically fails sight-required checks, own attacks have disadvantage, attacks against have advantage. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Full special-senses and vision interaction belongs to the stealth/vision pass. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 731, definition paragraph 732; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Burning **Preserved Core text:** Take fire damage at end of turn. An action, immersion, or successful Dexterity save ends it. **Effect:** At end of the affected creature's regular turn its generic record offers 1d4 fire damage to unified family arbitration, unless its source specifies another magnitude. Only the winning stack group deals damage. Damage immunity does not by itself remove Burning. **Application:** Applied only by an effect that explicitly inflicts Burning. Record the applying effect's DC; if none exists, use DC 10. **Duration and ending:** Self or adjacent helper may spend one Action to end all active ordinary-extinguishable attached fires on this creature. Full immersion of all burning portions does the same. Explicit protected-source exceptions survive. At each regular target turn end, after due ticks are consumed, each surviving active ongoing-fire record with future damage remaining makes its own binary DEX save against its own source DC or 10. Success ends only that record. An indefinite generic fire counts as having future damage; a finite record with its final tick consumed expires without another save. **Stacking:** Independent records enter unified ongoing-fire family arbitration. One Action/full immersion clears all ordinary-extinguishable records; DEX saves operate per surviving eligible record, not one selected-source save for all fires. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fire immunity prevents the damage but does not automatically end Burning unless the source or immunity says so. An effect explicitly immune to Burning blocks application. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: 1d4 fire fallback, source DC or 10, damage then free ending save; Action/immersion can end before damage. - NEW: shared periodic timing and strongest-record precedence; adjacent helper and immersion boundaries. - SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 733, definition paragraph 734; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Charmed **Preserved Core text:** Cannot willingly harm the charmer; charmer has advantage on social checks against it. **Effect:** The creature cannot willingly take an action or make a choice it knows would harm the charmer: this includes attacks, harmful targeting, and knowingly placing the charmer in a harmful area or indirect effect. Unforeseeable or genuinely unknown collateral harm is not retroactively a willing violation. The charmer has advantage on social ability checks against it. Charmed itself never compels affection, obedience, beliefs, allegiance, affirmative protection or self-harm. **Application:** Each application identifies the charmer/source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration and repeat-save/ending procedure. **Stacking:** A creature may be Charmed by more than one source; each source relation is tracked independently. Advantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Charm immunity prevents application. Forced actions from another effect are not made voluntary merely because the creature is Charmed. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies the creature cannot attack the charmer or target the charmer with harmful abilities or magical effects, and gives the charmer advantage on social interaction checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Agency clarification: Charmed never by itself grants control over beliefs, targets or decisions beyond the explicit harm restriction. - Source-faithful correction reviewed in GPT_CUSTOM_RIDER_SECOND_REVIEW.md: Core's unwilling-to-harm restriction is broader than direct targeting; preserve its area/indirect-harm scope without importing mind control. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 735, definition paragraph 736; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Corrupted **Preserved Core text:** Healing is reduced, corruption-sensitive effects worsen, and long rests may shift behavior or form until cleansed. **Effect:** Halve each healing effect's final potential HP once, rounded down, before the HP ceiling. Saves against spells/abilities from individually recorded Evil creatures have disadvantage; its aura can be detected by effects revealing evil. At each completed long rest make DC 15 WIS save or move one moral step Good to Neutral to Evil, leaving law/chaos unchanged. Already Evil remains Evil. Alignment does not compel conduct, party separation, PvP or automatic oathbreaking. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Corrupted apply it. **Duration and ending:** Persists until an explicit cleansing effect or the eight-hour cleansing project in CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md succeeds. Long rest alone does not cleanse it. At a simultaneous cleansing/rest endpoint, resolve cleansing first and make the Corrupted rest save only if it remains. **Stacking:** Corrupted does not stack with itself. Apply the generic half-healing reduction once; an effect does not halve again merely because it restates the same Corrupted penalty. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Natural-20 death-save recovery and recovered Stable 1-HP recovery are state-recovery rules rather than healing effects and still restore exactly 1 HP. Explicit cleansing or protection may override within scope. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: healing effects restore half normal HP; disadvantage on saves against spells/abilities from evil creatures; faint aura detectable by magic revealing evil; at end of each long rest make DC 15 Wisdom save or alignment shifts one step toward evil. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: round half healing down once; guaranteed death-save/Stable one-HP state recovery is not a healing effect. - Source-grounded: individual recorded alignment or Evil tag only; no ancestry/faction inference, forced behavior or automatic conduct violation. - NEW: generic cleansing project supplies a finite recovery route. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Cross-check separately reviewed corruption-sensitive transformations and specific restoration effects. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 737, definition paragraph 738; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Dazed **Preserved Core text:** Choose either action or movement on the turn, not both; no bonus action. **Effect:** On every affected turn, including extra turns, choose Action-mode (at most one Action total and no voluntary Speed expenditure or Dash) or Movement-mode (ordinary movement, no Action). Movement expressly included in the permitted Action still resolves. No Bonus Action; Reactions and concentration are unaffected. **Application:** Only an effect that explicitly inflicts Dazed applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's endpoint. Applies immediately: earlier voluntary movement that turn forbids further Actions; an earlier Action forbids further voluntary Speed expenditure; if both already occurred, neither may occur again. Do not undo completed events. Extra-Action grants cannot bypass the one-Action ceiling. **Stacking:** Multiple Dazed applications do not further reduce the turn; track only the longest/independent ending sources. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An immunity to Dazed blocks application. Forced movement is not voluntary movement and remains possible. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: immediate mid-turn handling, each extra turn gets its own mode, one-Action ceiling, explicit action-contained movement exception. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Interaction with future nonstandard action types if any are introduced. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 739, definition paragraph 740; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Deafened **Preserved Core text:** Cannot hear and fails hearing checks; verbal coordination may fail. **Effect:** The creature cannot hear and automatically fails checks that require hearing. It cannot satisfy a rule that specifically requires hearing another creature's command, warning, chant or audible signal. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Deafened apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end condition. **Stacking:** Multiple applications do not compound. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Deafened does not prevent the creature from speaking or supplying its own verbal components unless another condition such as Silenced applies. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches inability to hear and automatic failure of hearing-required checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Operational clarification: 'verbal coordination may fail' means hearing-dependent coordination requirements fail; no generic roll is added. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Future command/audible-coordination features must state whether hearing is required. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 741, definition paragraph 742; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Exhausted **Preserved Core text:** Use the six-level exhaustion track; effects are cumulative and level 6 is death. **Effect:** Track 0–6 cumulative levels: 1 disadvantage ability checks; 2 half Speed after flat changes; 3 disadvantage attacks and saves; 4 maximum HP max(1,floor(otherwise-applicable maximum/2)); 5 Speed zero; 6 death. **Application:** An effect that grants one or more Exhaustion levels increases the track by that amount, maximum 6, unless it explicitly sets a level instead. **Duration and ending:** Eligible beneficial eight-hour long rest removes one level under CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md, at most one generic removal per 24 hours. Source-specific prerequisites can block removal. Meeting a prerequisite such as Moisture Dependency immersion does not itself remove a level unless printed. **Stacking:** Levels add, maximum 6. Derive level-4 maximum from the otherwise-applicable current maximum, never a previously halved value. Clamp HP down when maximum decreases; raising maximum does not heal. Level-5 zero Speed overrides halving. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An explicit Exhaustion immunity blocks levels. Removing Exhaustion from a dead level-6 creature does not restore life; resurrection is still required. **Compatible V6/source details:** - Level 1: disadvantage on ability checks. - Level 2: Speed halved. - Level 3: disadvantage on attack rolls and saving throws. - Level 4: hit point maximum halved. - Level 5: Speed reduced to 0. - Level 6: death. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW: maximum-HP floor 1, recomputation/clamping and flat-Speed-before-halving order. - NEW: finite generic long-rest recovery; source-specific removal blocks remain. - Recovered V6: six cumulative level effects. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 743, definition paragraph 744; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Frightened **Preserved Core text:** Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. **Effect:** While the source of fear is visible/in line of sight, the creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. While Frightened it cannot willingly move closer to that source. **Application:** Each application records its fear source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration and repeat-save procedure. **Stacking:** Separate fear sources are tracked independently. Disadvantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fear immunity blocks application. Forced movement may move the creature closer because the prohibition is on willing movement. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight, and prohibits willingly moving closer. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 745, definition paragraph 746; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Grappled **Preserved Core text:** Speed 0; ends if grappler is incapacitated or reach is broken. **Effect:** Speed becomes 0 and cannot be increased by bonuses while Grappled. **Application:** A Grappled application records the grappler/source and its reach. **Duration and ending:** Ends if the grappler is Incapacitated, reach breaks, or the applying effect ends/its escape succeeds. A class/spell card with a fixed save DC uses an Action and STR (Athletics) or DEX (Acrobatics) against that DC. An ordinary V6 grapple uses an Action to escape with STR (Athletics) or DEX (Acrobatics) opposed by the grappler's STR (Athletics); higher total wins, ties retain the grapple. Multiple grapplers require ending each relationship. **Stacking:** Multiple grapplers may maintain separate Grappled records; Speed remains 0 until all relevant grapples end. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A creature immune to Grappled cannot receive it. Teleportation or forced movement that breaks reach ends that grapple unless a specific effect says otherwise. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 adds that the creature cannot benefit from bonuses to Speed and confirms ending when the grappler is incapacitated or an effect removes the target from reach. - V6 all-XML paragraph 8206 gives ordinary grapple application and opposed escape; fixed-DC card escapes remain specific class/spell rules. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Final generic grapple/shove procedure remains part of the combat maneuver audit. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 747, definition paragraph 748; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json). ## Incapacitated **Preserved Core text:** Cannot take actions or reactions. **Effect:** The creature cannot take an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Passive effects continue unless their own rules require consciousness or another condition disables them. Incapacitated by itself does not reduce Speed or prohibit speech. **Application:** Applied by a condition or effect that explicitly says the creature is Incapacitated. **Duration and ending:** Use the parent condition/effect's duration. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Current shared concentration rules end concentration immediately when the creature becomes Incapacitated. A specific effect may preserve a passive benefit through Incapacitation if explicitly stated. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot take actions or reactions. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW integration: Bonus Actions are included in unavailable actions. - Already explicit in CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md: becoming Incapacitated ends concentration. preparedExcerpts.heading: Shared handling
preparedExcerpts.exactText:
## Shared handling

This overlay governs generic conditions in the combined candidate. A reviewed card overrides a generic clause only where it prints the specific exception. An unreviewed historical summary never grants an extra ability or bypasses a gate. The existing combined source-character/target/encounter hard-denial cap still applies to class/spell/companion applications.

Record each condition source, affected creature, applying DC, magnitude, start, duration and ending method. Same-name nonnumeric penalties apply once; independent sources continue until each ends. A generic cure naming a condition clears its source records unless a reviewed procedure specifies one-record scope. Bleeding Medicine and Burning DEX saves use the specific procedures below. Track Charmed, Frightened, Marked and Grappled relationships separately. Exhaustion, Intoxication, Unity and Wounds use their explicit tracks.

Immunity to a named condition prevents that condition, including an inherited component, but does not silently grant immunity to every parent condition that can cause it. For example, Prone immunity prevents the Prone component of Unconscious, not its other effects. Immunity to an inflicted condition never erases the underlying zero-HP or dead state. Gaining immunity suppresses applicable existing effects while immunity lasts; their clocks continue unless explicitly paused. Removing immunity does not reapply a one-time consequence or restart an old duration.

Advantages and disadvantages never multiply dice: any advantage and any disadvantage cancel to one normal d20 roll, regardless of the number of sources. Automatic failure of a required check/save is resolved without a roll. A condition does not give a save where its source grants none. A critical-if-hit rider never makes a missed attack hit. Automatic failure has no rolled total: use ordinary Failure, not Critical Failure or an invented failure margin, unless the source explicitly supplies one.

Generic Core Bleeding and Burning join family.bleeding and family.ongoing-fire respectively, with source-owner stack groups. At one identical target timing marker, all due generic and custom groups in that family compete: highest expected unmitigated damage, then earliest application. Only the winning group's source-permitted instances deal damage. All due groups consume that tick; losers do not defer or bank it. Different printed markers resolve separately. No record also receives a duplicate generic tick. Core generic timing is end of regular target turn; extra turns do not tick. Outside initiative preserve one periodic step per complete six seconds with no duplicate interval across initiative transitions.

Strain is not globally unique: expedition.strain and warrior.serum-strain are separate source-qualified tracks, both distinct from the six-level Exhaustion condition. See the Strain namespace reference for the current candidate. Oracle one-turn Revelation backlash is also separate from global Exhaustion; its printed penalties and endpoint remain unchanged. Wound Eater feeding failures explicitly use global Exhaustion. Never silently convert similarly named tracks.

See CONDITION_RECOVERY_PLAYTEST.md for finite recovery, cleansing, substance, Intoxication and Unity procedures. These new proposals are labeled separately from recovered source rules. Conditions do not reveal Director secrets or force player beliefs or decisions.

SUPERSESSION — NEW PROVISIONAL INTEGRATION: The unified Bleeding/ongoing-fire family registry supersedes earlier provisional clauses that selected generic records separately, used ending DC as a damage tie-breaker, cleared all generic Bleeding through one Medicine result, or used one Burning save to clear all generic Burning. Original Core quotations and raw review history remain unchanged. See CUSTOM_CONDITION_BINDINGS.md and the recorded GPT_GENERIC_CUSTOM_ALIGNMENT review.

It cannot satisfy a rule that specifically requires hearing another creature's command, warning, chant or audible signal. **Application:** Only effects that explicitly inflict Deafened apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end condition. **Stacking:** Multiple applications do not compound. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Deafened does not prevent the creature from speaking or supplying its own verbal components unless another condition such as Silenced applies. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches inability to hear and automatic failure of hearing-required checks. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Operational clarification: 'verbal coordination may fail' means hearing-dependent coordination requirements fail; no generic roll is added. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Future command/audible-coordination features must state whether hearing is required. preparedExcerpts.heading: Frightened
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Frightened **Preserved Core text:** Disadvantage while source is visible and cannot willingly move closer. **Effect:** While the source of fear is visible/in line of sight, the creature has disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls. While Frightened it cannot willingly move closer to that source. **Application:** Each application records its fear source. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration and repeat-save procedure. **Stacking:** Separate fear sources are tracked independently. Disadvantage does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Fear immunity blocks application. Forced movement may move the creature closer because the prohibition is on willing movement. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 specifies disadvantage on ability checks and attack rolls while the source of fear is within line of sight, and prohibits willingly moving closer. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 745, definition paragraph 746; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

preparedExcerpts.heading: Incapacitated
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Incapacitated **Preserved Core text:** Cannot take actions or reactions. **Effect:** The creature cannot take an Action, Bonus Action or Reaction. Passive effects continue unless their own rules require consciousness or another condition disables them. Incapacitated by itself does not reduce Speed or prohibit speech. **Application:** Applied by a condition or effect that explicitly says the creature is Incapacitated. **Duration and ending:** Use the parent condition/effect's duration. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Current shared concentration rules end concentration immediately when the creature becomes Incapacitated. A specific effect may preserve a passive benefit through Incapacitation if explicitly stated. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 matches: cannot take actions or reactions. **Explicit integration decisions:** - NEW integration: Bonus Actions are included in unavailable actions. - Already explicit in CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md: becoming Incapacitated ends concentration. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 749, definition paragraph 750; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

preparedExcerpts.heading: Invisible
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Invisible **Preserved Core text:** Cannot be seen normally; attacks against it have disadvantage and its attacks have advantage until location is revealed. **Effect:** Cannot be seen normally. Until an observer knows its location, that observer attacks it with disadvantage and it attacks that observer with advantage. Once location is revealed, these Invisible-specific modifiers end for that observer. Do not re-grant them through V6 generic unseen rules solely because it is still Invisible. A special sense actually seeing it bypasses these modifiers. Knowing location is not seeing; effects requiring sight still need sight. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly granting Invisible applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the granting effect's duration. V6 attacks reveal location upon attacking; resolve the revealing attack first, then observers able to perceive evidence know the location. Independent hiding/concealment uses its own procedure; later broad vision integration must specify losing and regaining location knowledge. Invisible remains visually effective after revelation. **Stacking:** Multiple Invisible effects do not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** A special sense or magic that actually sees the creature removes Invisible's unseen benefits for that observer within that sense's scope. Knowing location is not the same as seeing. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: impossible to see without special senses or magic; heavily obscured for hiding; location may be detected by noises or tracks; attacks against have disadvantage and own attacks have advantage. **Source conflicts:** - Core explicitly ends the generic attack advantage/disadvantage when location is revealed; V6 states those attack modifiers without that endpoint. Core controls the conflict. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Operational distinction: visibility state and known location are separate. - No generic detection DC, automatic attack-reveal rule or movement-rehide rule is invented here. - Recovered V6: attacking reveals location. NEW timing clarification: resolve that attack before its revelation; Core location endpoint specifically overrides the otherwise-conflicting unseen attack modifiers. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Stealth, sound, tracks, hiding and location-reveal procedure in the vision/stealth pass. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 753, definition paragraph 754; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

preparedExcerpts.heading: Prone
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Prone **Preserved Core text:** Crawl or stand; melee attackers within 5 ft. have advantage; ranged attackers have disadvantage. **Effect:** Own attacks have disadvantage. Melee attacks against it within 5 feet have advantage; ranged attacks against it have disadvantage at every distance; other attacks beyond 5 feet have disadvantage. Movement requires crawling or standing. Drop Prone without Speed expenditure; standing costs half current Speed, rounded down, requires nonzero Speed and sufficient movement. Crawl costs 2 feet per foot, or 3 in difficult terrain. **Application:** Applied when an effect explicitly knocks a creature Prone or another rule such as Unconscious causes it. **Duration and ending:** Ends when the creature successfully stands or an explicit effect ends Prone. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Prone immunity blocks application. A feature may explicitly ignore Prone attack penalties. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6: only movement is crawl unless standing; own attack rolls have disadvantage; attacks from within 5 feet have advantage, otherwise disadvantage. **Source conflicts:** - For a ranged attack made from within 5 feet, V6 distance-only wording would grant advantage while Core specifically says ranged attackers have disadvantage. Core controls. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Core-vs-V6 conflict resolved in favor of Core for ranged attacks within 5 feet. - Recovered V6 movement: half-Speed standing and 2/3-for-1 crawling. NEW explicit zero-Speed standing prohibition, preventing zero-cost standing while Grappled. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 763, definition paragraph 764; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

preparedExcerpts.heading: Restrained
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Restrained **Preserved Core text:** Speed 0; attacks against have advantage, own attacks and Dexterity saves have disadvantage. **Effect:** Speed becomes 0 and cannot benefit from Speed bonuses. Attack rolls against the creature have advantage; its own attack rolls and Dexterity saving throws have disadvantage. **Application:** Only an effect explicitly inflicting Restrained applies it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's printed duration, save or escape rule. If an effect creates a physical restraint and provides no escape procedure, use the existing shared playtest escape procedure only if that source is eligible for it. **Stacking:** Multiple Restrained applications do not compound penalties, but all independently maintained sources must end before the creature is no longer Restrained. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** Restrained immunity blocks application. Teleportation does not automatically end a restraint unless it breaks the source relationship or the applying effect says so. **Compatible V6/source details:** - V6 adds that the creature cannot benefit from bonuses to Speed. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Final generic physical-restraint escape procedure in combat rules. Provenance: Core V2 `books/player/Decennium_Descent_Core_Systems_Bible_v2_Known_Descent.docx`, zero-based all-XML heading paragraph 767, definition paragraph 768; both positions, exact text and book SHA-256 are verified against the approved book and retained in the [condition data](../../data/playtest/condition_playtests.json).

preparedExcerpts.heading: Silenced
preparedExcerpts.exactText: ## Silenced **Preserved Core text:** Cannot use verbal components, command words, Chants, or audible coordination. **Effect:** The creature cannot use spell/ability verbal components, command words, Chants, or any feature requiring audible coordination. It may still think, perceive, move, use somatic/nonverbal abilities and use effects that explicitly function without sound. **Application:** Only effects explicitly inflicting Silenced apply it. **Duration and ending:** Use the applying effect's duration/end rule. **Stacking:** Does not stack. **Immunities and specific exceptions:** An ability explicitly usable without speech or audible sound is unaffected. Silence immunity blocks application only if explicitly defined. **Explicit integration decisions:** - Clarification: Silenced is not universal mental or magical shutdown. **Remaining wider integration work:** - Specific audible-command features must state whether they require being heard by recipients.
