# Maximum HP, stat changes and HP thresholds

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED —58 exact passages:51 class records and7 feats.** The [source register](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_BINDINGS.md) preserves the original procedures; [source validation](MAXIMUM_HP_SOURCE_VALIDATION.json) verifies equality and hashes. The [first captured notebook reply](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FIRST_REVIEW_PARTIAL.md) is incomplete and must be read with the [complete tail and boundary corrections](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_BOUNDARIES.md) and [exact implementation closure](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_MAXIMUM_HP_FINAL_CLOSURE.md).

These rules cover the maximum-HP and threshold components supplied here. They do not promote whole feats, create companion actions, decide character advancement, or certify every monster/item/spell maximum-HP modifier.

## Recompute capacity from separate records

Keep base maximum, bonuses, reductions and systemic multipliers separate. Base maximum excludes all modifiers represented separately in this ledger. Never feed a previously modified maximum back into the formula.

First calculate the otherwise-applicable maximum:

    preSystemicMaximum = max(1, baseMaximum + compatibleBonuses − strongestMonkTrauma)

Then apply the reviewed systemic factors against that same value:

    effectiveMaximum = max(1, floor(preSystemicMaximum × systemicFactors))

Expedition Strain4+ contributes3/4 and Exhaustion4+ contributes1/2. Multiply compatible rational factors before rounding once. Base101, Flesh Warden+20, Monk trauma−9 and both factors produce42. Suppressing that trauma produces45; do not subtract the trauma again afterward.

The numerical modifier calculation does not perform lethal-track transitions. Use the separate reviewed life-state procedure when a track actually changes. Merely recomputing maximum HP must not re-kill a living collapsed survivor at track6.

Each application retains its own ID, source, owner, target, magnitude, start/end markers, presence and suppression state, arbitration group and any acquisition/creation snapshot needed for its formula. Keep records even when another stronger application wins. Suppression does not stop clocks.

## Bonuses and source identities

| Source | Bonus and update rule |
|---|---|
| Flesh Warden | +2 per Warrior level while legally equipped; capacity only |
| Wizard Conjuration specialization | +Wizard level captured when that Wizard spell creates the summon |
| Flesh Ascendant | +2 per current Wizard level of the eligible controller supplying the feature |
| Familiar Bond | Provisional +current eligible owner's character level to familiar maximum HP |
| Tenacity | +current character level |
| Tough | +twice character level when the feat was acquired; retain this snapshot |
| Tough as Nails | +2 per character level at acquisition, then +2 for each later level |
| Dark Fortitude | +2 per current character level |

**New feat integration:** distinct feat identities granting maximum HP add together unless an explicit source says otherwise. Duplicate copies of the same feat do not add. Their original acquisition/prerequisite, retraining and other-effect rules still need their separate review.

**New Wizard-specific stacking exception:** Conjuration and Flesh Ascendant add when the same undead summon qualifies for both, overriding the frozen strongest same-stat class-technique bonus default for this pair only. Flesh Ascendant's engine[24] and named card describe one modifier identity; do not count both.

When later companion lifecycle code constructs records, the engine/card aliases must share one actual effect identity, including suppression and removal. Numerical non-stacking alone must not leave a second textual alias operative after that effect is suppressed.

Conjuration's amount and caster provenance stay tied to creation. A later caster level or controller change does not recompute that snapshot. Flesh Ascendant instead follows the current eligible controller; changing control ends the old controller's eligibility and can create the new controller's eligible bonus, without healing.

**New Familiar Bond interpretation:** its ambiguous “gains hit points” wording supplies maximum capacity. Initial creation under that bonus can include it in starting HP; later level increases add capacity only. Familiar ownership/replacement and attack/command rules remain in the future companion package.

When a creature is initially created, construct its starting state from its final creation maximum unless its source expressly enters it damaged. Base20 plus Conjuration10 plus Flesh Ascendant20 gives50/50 at creation. Acquiring either bonus later does not fill missing HP. No bonus changes creature or command caps.

## Monk trauma uses one global strongest reduction

**Explicit correction of the earlier per-owner proposal:** Monk engine[9]'s categorical non-stacking clause controls. Use the largest currently operative Monk maximum-HP reduction on the target across all owners.

Ribcrusher applies S+M, Bone-Breaking Strike2S+M, and Deathless Silence4S+M. Preserve each successful application separately, including repeated applications of the same card. Do not combine the strongest magnitude with another record's longer duration. If−9 is suppressed, an operative−5 can become effective; when−5 expires, it stops contributing even while−9 remains suppressed.

Default Monk trauma ends when the target completes a short or long rest. This is effect removal, independent of how many numerical rest rewards the target already earned. Interrupted rest ends none. A genuinely explicit earlier/different endpoint controls its own record; the existence of an endpoint parameter does not grant permission to invent one.

Deathless Silence has three independent components: the Monk's protection from Reactions/opportunity attacks through source-next-regular-start; target defensive-passive suppression through that target's next-turn end; and maximum-HP trauma through the target's completed rest. Preserve the already reviewed control clocks.

## Capacity changes are not HP damage or healing

After any maximum change, clamp current normal HP down only if it exceeds the new maximum. Adding/restoring maximum HP gives no current HP. This clamp is not damage, sacrifice or healing; it creates no Wound save, death-save failure, resource trigger, redirection or first-fall event. Decay does not prevent capacity restoration.

Temporary HP is independent and remains unchanged. Maximum reduced to10 does not remove an existing25 temporary HP.

Dead, Stable and dying0 creatures retain their life state, counters and Stable deadline. A minimum maximum of1 never revives a corpse. Critical's healing ceiling recomputes afterward as max(1,effectiveMaximum−1); it is not another maximum-HP reduction.

## Exact thresholds and recorded events

Use effective maximum and integer comparison, without rounding a percentage threshold first:

| Wording | Comparison |
|---|---|
| At/below one-quarter | 4×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below one-quarter | 4×HP < maximum |
| At/below half | 2×HP ≤ maximum |
| Below half | 2×HP < maximum |
| Above half | 2×HP > maximum |

Continuous predicates update whenever HP or maximum changes: Wyrmhide, Brutality Sense, Pain Empowerment, Dark Fortitude's poison resistance, Life Drinker's conditional damage, and “below maximum” regeneration eligibility. Pain Empowerment uses full10% missing-HP bands, capped at+5, at its printed pre-roll moment.

**New first-fall interpretation:** Anointed Guardian, Burning Blood IV, Death's Threshold and Adrenal Floodgate require a genuine downward crossing. At/below-quarter triggers require HP moving from above quarter to at/below quarter. Burning Blood IV requires moving from at/above half to strictly below half. Actual damage or direct HP loss can establish a crossing unless a source specifically restricts it to damage. Capacity changes and clamps cannot.

If a rest refreshes a first-fall use while its subject is already below the threshold, neither the refresh nor another1HP loss fires it. The subject must return to the non-trigger side and cross again. Source frequency/history remains a separate eligibility gate; a crossing alone grants no new use.

Death's Threshold's exit requires actual HP restoration leaving the creature above half. A maximum reduction that makes unchanged HP above half does not end it. A later actual heal can satisfy that exit even if the creature was already above half before that heal.

**New continuous duration interpretation:** Mythic Carapace and Butcherform Chassis end when active and strictly below quarter. A maximum increase can therefore end them without damage. Exact quarter remains legal. Other duration endpoints still apply.

Record pre/post normal HP and the event-effective maximum for historical checks. Rewind Wound uses the maximum stored with its referenced damage event, never a later maximum. Freeze same-event HP crossings before a later stat clamp.

Rewind Wound requires genuine damage causing actual normal-HP decrease and leaving the target below half; it does not require a first crossing. HP40→30 at maximum100 qualifies even though both values are below half. An event entirely absorbed by temporary HP does not qualify.

Selection/rider timing follows each card: Mass Healing Light when its target is chosen; Merciful Sacrament at initial activation; Flesh to Ash before rolling damage; Death Touch at strike start; Blessing of the Meek/ Verdant Pulse before healing; Final Verdict at legal targeting; Fearbrand/Malicious Execution before their damage/rider; Echo Strike after its copied damage. Brutality Progress's already reviewed snapshot rules remain unchanged.

## Percentage recovery and damage

Use effective maximum when the amount resolves unless the source explicitly references an earlier snapshot. Floor the percentage amount, with minimum1 only where printed or already supplied by the reviewed viable-resurrection bridge.

Wound Eater III can heal0 at maximum3. Spiral III and False Life V explicitly retain minimum1 for quarter recovery. Unyielding Light uses one third with minimum1. Divine Rebirth uses the reviewed viable-return max(1,floor(maximum/2)). Wound Eater V's quarter target-HP loss and half self-heal cap retain their direct-loss classification. Ledger Unbound caps its raw damage at a quarter of target maximum before its save-halving.

Repair Pulse and Snap Rebuild use half device maximum under their own functional/destroyed target rules. A tiny-maximum reconstruction's viability belongs to the device lifecycle and is not silently converted into a general minimum1 here.

## Attack damage before Monk trauma

**New integration for the supplied Monk trauma cards:** choose/pay an after-hit option at its legal hit window. Resolve the ordinary attack's damage, Wounds, Instant Death and any survival replacement against the pre-trauma maximum; freeze its metrics. If the target remains an eligible living creature, resolve the trauma CON save using its then-current save modifier, including applicable Wound consequences. On failure, create the trauma record and recompute capacity.

If the attack leaves the target Dead, no combat-trauma record is needed and the paid cost is not refunded. A legal same-resolution death replacement preserving life can leave the target eligible.

Example: maximum30, HP30; damage4 leaves26 and records4 actual damage. A later−15 maximum reduction gives maximum15 and clamps current HP26→15. The11-point clamp causes no second damage/Wound/threshold event and cannot rewrite the attack's Instant Death threshold or concentration packet.

## Validation and remaining scope

The current reference passes60 targeted checks and909 systemic parity states. It accepts already legal source records and event snapshots; it does not decide source acquisition, perform companion creation, pay Ki, schedule turns or consume first-fall uses.

Still open: unsupplied item/spell/monster/disease/curse maximum modifiers; non-Monk reductions; exceptions applying after systemic multipliers; full feat acquisition/retraining; familiar and summon/control lifecycle; unusual device reconstruction; human balance. The58-source discussion does not close these larger domains.

# Advanced crafting — player candidate guide

**REVIEWED — authored operational PLAYTEST.** Use this guide with the Enchanting, Rune Carving, Scribing and Tinkering candidate cards and their body catalogue. Each card supplies its actual numbers, ingredients, formula access, station and work time. This guide supplies the common procedures. A recipe name, price or ingredient mention grants no unprinted power or automatic access to stock.

## Make one recorded work order

Choose the recipe and one permitted complete body model and size before starting. Reserve `floor(1.5 × printed quantity)` actual complete ordinary bodies in a fixed order. These bodies are additional to all printed process components and required working implements. They must never have been magically altered, must have positive HP and remain complete, and cannot simultaneously serve another order, a consumed ingredient or the working toolkit. An ordinary weapon or armor suit retains its genuinely established grade and permitted physical history. Fixed carriers use Standard grade. Automaton chassis must be unmodified, unflawed ordinary B5 chassis, with Tiny or Small chosen before work.

All maximum-yield reserves must still qualify immediately before the single completion roll, even if Standard would use fewer. Missing, Broken, incomplete or committed reserves pause work. Lawful pre-roll repair or replacement retains that entry's position and records its actual history. There is no post-roll substitution, purchase or choice of the best bodies. Transform the first resolved number of bodies; unused ones remain their actual mundane stock. Failed or Mishap transforms none, although a genuine mishap can damage stock. Returning unused bodies is not ingredient recovery.

The actual creator, station and safe storage must accommodate the work. Reserves can occupy separate lawful storage while each body is worked sequentially; they need not all fit on one bench. Source ingredients remain required for the whole printed batch, not once for each output. Their mass does not produce extra complete bodies or get added again to each output. Preserve physical identity, compatible containment, damage, losses and material age throughout.

## Training, access and work

All four trades are artisan creation using INT. Their primary credentials are Enchanter's tools, Runecarver's tools, Calligrapher's supplies and Tinker's tools respectively. Add one actually applicable PB, or replacing expertise, rather than adding numerical trade level. An untrained character can attempt an otherwise eligible level 1–4 recipe without tool PB and with disadvantage. Trained recipe eligibility is `max(4, trade level)`, with actual source/formula access. Recipes above level 4 still require the required formula. Possession of a finished item teaches neither its formula nor its trade.

Use the card's real station and auxiliary implements. A complete ordinary toolkit can supply the ordinary implements actually inside it; it does not also supply expensive tiered ingredients or a workstation. Source facilities and ordinary tools give no automatic bonus. An actually available compatible facility uses the established rental baseline of 1 gp per eight reserved hours. Paying that rate does not create capacity or permission.

These creation cards have `fieldCraftable=false`. A historical `timeMode=field` label does not waive that flag. An expedition worksite still needs the genuine fortified/research-site permission and fixed required facility. Other workshop, Haven and longer-term permissions retain their own requirements. Only eligible assistants within the card's limit can assist; they must work all required hours, do not shorten the order and receive no assistant crafting XP.

An actually eligible Forge Dwarf multiplies creation time by 0.75, rounding up once to a whole minute, and treats a Standard creation result as Exceptional. This changes neither access nor ingredients. It does not reduce repair, servicing, research, encoding, attunement, ordinary calendar waits or rest. Respect the two-active-work-Watch limit and actual rest restrictions; the same hours cannot also count as guard duty, travel, another job or beneficial rest.

The first stable phase is `min(15 minutes, adjusted total active creation time)` and is included in the printed total. Preregister later phases of at most eight active hours. Completed phases stabilize only the actual eligible incorporated inputs. Raw stock and a recoverable catalyst keep their own age and protection requirements. Interruption loses unfinished-phase progress, not costs, completed phases or physical history. Ineligible inputs pause the order; unfinished work has no active item power.

Use the existing crafting framework's first-success, repeat, qualified-failure and triviality rules. The card preserves its exact progression and capped trivial threshold. Using, repairing, servicing or studying an item does not award that recipe's creation XP. Formula research and ordinary formula copying keep their own reviewed procedures.

## Resolve the six creation outcomes

| Margin against the recipe DC | Outcome | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 10 or more | Masterwork | `floor(1.5Q)` outputs, or Q with the structural option; at most one eligible catalyst unit retained |
| 5–9 | Exceptional | `floor(1.25Q)` outputs, or Q with the structural option |
| 0–4 | Standard | Q outputs |
| −1 to −4 | Flawed | `floor(Q/2)` when Q≥2; see singleton rules below |
| −5 to −9 | Failed | No output; bounded ingredient recovery |
| −10 or worse, or natural 1 | Mishap | No output; consumed materials lost and the actual tradeskill mishap procedure applies |

A natural 20 adds no extra manufacturing-band shift. The Forge Dwarf adjustment changes Standard to Exceptional only. Choose the permitted yield or structural option once for the batch. It never improves charges, damage, DC, spell rank, service count, research potency, carrying capacity or other magical properties.

For a structural object, the Exceptional/Masterwork alternative retains Q outputs with P25/P50 workmanship. Use its actual ordinary B after legitimate size and grade, and only the strongest existing or newly selected percentage. Maximum HP is `B + max(1, floor(B×P/100))` for positive P; otherwise B. Apply one persistent flaw last: `max(1, floor(improved maximum/2))`. Retain the old damage deficit, `old maximum − old current`, and subtract it from the new maximum, clamped to [0, new maximum]. Standard does not heal. At B5, unflawed maxima are 5/6/7; flawed maxima are 2/3/3. At B1 they are 1/2/2 and 1/1/1.

A structural Q1 Flawed result creates one persistently flawed item, which can finish Broken if retained damage reaches its reduced maximum. Q≥2 Flawed only reduces yield and retains actual prior flaws; producing one output from that batch does not add a singleton flaw. No extra duration penalty is invented for these durable carriers. Repair does not erase the flaw or repeat the workmanship increase.

Automata are the explicit creature exception. Their printed creature AC and HP never increase from structural quality. Choosing the alternative simply retains Q with a quality label and no mechanical improvement. Q1 Flawed maps to Failed, including that failure's recovery procedure. Q≥2 keeps the reduced yield. A produced automaton starts at `max(1, floor(printed creature HP × latest chassis current HP / 5))`; a full chassis produces full printed HP. This is a creation conversion, not level scaling or a second structural track.

## Inputs, retained tools and failure returns

Keep every component occurrence separate, including repeated catalog IDs. Its consumed flag and role govern what happens. An expensive object labeled tool can be a consumed process input; it cannot also be the retained working implement. A price, core/essence title or material description does not make it a catalyst.

Masterwork may retain at most one actual unit total from an eligible consumed catalyst occurrence on that recipe, chosen after the check. It must have participated nondestructively until retention is resolved. The returned unit retains identity, age, condition and compatible vessel; it is not also a second embedded core in an output.

On Failed creation, for each eligible exact consumed non-catalyst input identity, recover at most one quarter of its fixed consumed-input quantity for this batch, capped by the eligible amount actually remaining from those same inputs, and rounded down once to that identity's legal source-unit precision. Do not take one quarter of the surviving remainder. Previously returned, forfeited or lost quantities and unrelated stock cannot fund this recovery. For each exact eligible identity in this batch, use `recovered_i = u_i × floor(min(Q_i / 4, R_i) / u_i)`. Q_i is its fixed consumed-input quantity; R_i is the eligible amount surviving from those same inputs; u_i is its legal source-unit precision. Group only genuinely identical eligible inputs within this same batch while retaining every physical occurrence. Catalysts and unrelated batches do not enter that recovery group. The expressly divisible bulk profiles are Enchanting Veilthread; Rune Carving Runic ink and Binding agent; Scribing Ink and Preservation treatment. They use 0.01 of their exact source unit only when actually supplied in that divisible form. Other stones, lenses, matrices, glyph pieces, parchment/cover/binding units, hardware packs, cells and consumed tools are indivisible unless their own genuine independent profile permits subdivision. No quarter-lens, value conversion, remainder banking or second salvage pass over failed waste.

Mishap or abandonment returns no consumed inputs. Nonconsumed tools and unused reserved bodies remain only as they actually survive. Existing gathering, preservation, finite-matter and exclusive-debris histories still apply. A public ingredient mention does not disclose a donor dossier, grant acquisition rights, supply missing metadata or make the required stock free.

## Structure, state and repair

The body catalogue gives complete physical bodies, primary members, dimensions, hands and capacity. Structural AC protects the item, not its bearer. Ordinary equipment targeting, actual damage compatibility and carried-item protection still apply. One aggregate HP track does not give each screw, page or limb a second independently targetable pool. A name or a flag does not establish intact structure.

Magic requires an actual complete positive-HP, accessible, unmelded, unsuppressed participating item. Required hands, legal bearing positions and line of effect remain mandatory. Suppression removes magical functions but leaves otherwise lawful ordinary physical functions. A suppressed automaton is inert; its paid operating time continues. A stowed or closed reference cannot help a check. Later suppression never reverses completed healing, damage or ordinary work.

Initialize each physical output's stated budget once at lawful completion, even if a structural Flawed output finishes Broken. Repair can expose its existing budget but never initialize it again. Separate outputs have separate budgets; copies, snapshots and changed display IDs are not new items. Record actual campaign time, phase/sequence, canonical activation/check identity, custody and expenditures. Invalid declarations spend nothing. Once a legal activation commits, misses, resistance, prevention, interruption or later loss of eligibility do not refund its costs.

Ordinary advanced restoration requires training in the recipe's primary credential, INT, its real compatible station and original required repair implements. Enchanted weapon/armor restoration also needs actual host-compatible fixtures/tools. This permission does not teach Smithing or manufacture a missing host. A broken target cannot serve as its own missing toolkit.

| Restoration | DC | Active work | Actual material reference |
|---|---|---|---|
| Functional positive-HP body | 10 | `max(1 hour, recorded maximumHP/10 hours)` | 25% of admitted undamaged mundane body reference |

# Transformation and Harmonic Bulwark playtest rules

**REVIEWED / reference-VALIDATED within the five-spell scope.** This guide supplies five promoted operational-playtest overlays and twelve finite forms. The catalog now contains83 operational drafts and765 unfinished spells. The candidate versions remain preserved as review history. Original spells, class access, printed schools, base RP and the frozen class packet remain preserved. All new boundaries below are provisional design decisions agreed in the notebook, not recovered original rules. Numerical balance and table playtesting remain outstanding.

## Cast summary

All five use an Action and V/S/F. Ordinary known/prepared access, class-level gates, base RP, component legality, Dissonance/Refrain, exact class modifications, countering and concentration damage checks remain mandatory.

|---|---|---:|---|
| Harmonic Bulwark |60ft; one willing perceived creature|5 plus chosen X|Cast instantaneous; accepted shield to depletion/replacement/recipient's completed long rest|
| Polymorph |60ft; one perceived physical creature|7|Concentration60seconds|
| Shapechange |Self|26|Concentration60seconds|
| True Polymorph |120ft; one eligible physical creature or discrete object|26|Concentration60seconds, then until dispelled without concentration|
| Mass Polymorph |120ft;1–10 distinct perceived physical creatures|26|One concentration record,60seconds|

These are the selected spells' unchanged base costs; exact class access is read from the preserved catalog. Shapechange's printed120-foot source field remains in provenance; operational Self is explicitly NEW. Harmonic Bulwark's Action/range/components are NEW design, not a proven merge with the older Mana Shield name.

Before paying, choose legal targets, output profiles/templates and all spatial placements. For a concentration spell, account for the original anatomy that will return when your own old concentration ends. That projected anatomy must still be eligible for the prospective cast. Check all costs and components. Then:

1. Commit Action and actual RP payment, with ordinary class cadence consequences.
2. End your previous concentration, including all remaining Mass links, even if the new spell subsequently fails.
3. Resolve countering and initial saves. No post-commit refund.
4. Apply successful transformations. An anatomy maintained by another source persists until a successful legal replacement. No displaced anatomy remains underneath the new form.

Beginning an unrelated concentration spell does not end an already permanent True Polymorph. Starting any new concentration spell must use the shared concentration ledger, including spells outside this packet.

## Harmonic Bulwark

Choose additional conversion payment X from0 through current PB before commitment. The shield offered to the chosen recipient is **5 × (actual base RP paid + X)**. An exact legal discount can reduce the base payment. X is additional, actually paid and never discounted. Dissonance or other surcharge payments add no shield credit. Refrain affects post-cast Dissonance under ordinary rules; this spell invents no immediate Refrain surcharge.

A zero-credit fresh cast is illegal. Free casts do not mint shield value. An exact effect copying an already-resolved buffer event needs its own explicit permission. Pay Action, actual cast cost and X before countering and the normal strongest-only comparison. A stronger or equal existing shield stays, but the entire payment remains spent. A countered spell produces no offer. The accepted shield belongs to the recipient, does not heal, and normally ends at that recipient's next completed long rest.

Example: actual base payment3, X2 and surcharge2 costs7RP and offers25temporaryHP. It does not offer35. If the recipient already has25 or more, their current grant stays with its original lifetime.

## Identity, attack statistics and equipment

Keep one physical identity and one current/max HP ledger, current temporary-HP grant, Wounds/injuries, death state, conditions, actual attributes, PB, class resources, rest/recharge uses, initiative, concentration and independent effect clocks. A form is never a second HP pool. Body matter lost or destroyed remains lost. Existing class abilities use the subject's normal statistics when anatomy permits them.

The transformed subject owns its attacks, damage and kills. Polymorph, Mass and Shapechange supplied attacks use the original caster's **current** spell attack and M=max(1, casting modifier). True snapshots caster spell attack, DC, PB, M and source class at casting, throughout shaping and permanence. Supplied natural attacks are not spell casts and do not automatically trigger caster “your spell deals damage,” spell-kill or per-cast resource features.

Creature-origin subjects retain their original creature-type, ancestry, class and soul identity. Object-origin manifestations have the `transformed-object` origin tag; profile names grant no humanoid/beast/elemental/undead tag. Immutable earliest origin follows every chain of transformations and control changes.

Original carried/equipped gear melds into a record and is unavailable for ordinary weapon/shield/component use. Compatible certified passive bonuses may remain. A handed form can acquire and use real external gear normally. On an internal Shapechange switch, keep compatible external items and drop incompatible items in the current space or nearest legal adjacent space; never add them to the old meld set. Dropped items remain there.

When a different successful transformation replaces a record, atomically close the old record, restore its still-existing original meld set, include legitimate currently equipped external items, and capture that resulting gear as the new record's meld set. There is no intervening action/reaction/targeting window. Destroyed, consumed, dropped or lost items are never recreated. This also applies when a spell ends a Druid form. Suppression is not record closure and never recaptures gear. Original melded gear remains inaccessible while suppressed, including weapons, armor and material components. External gear remains real and usable only when root anatomy is certified compatible.

## Initial saves, repeats and agency

Polymorph, Mass and True creature→creature allow a willing recipient to waive the initial CON save. Otherwise resolve CON against the original caster's current DC (True uses its casting snapshot). Success leaves the target unchanged. Exact transformation immunity and legendary defenses still apply.

Each unwilling transformed target may repeat that save at each original regular-turn end, and after the first event in each numbered round that causes **positive actual normal HP damage**, after all prevention and temporary HP. Temporary-HP-only loss does not qualify. Each target has a separate round ledger; a recast does not create a second damage-triggered save from the same round. Finish the actual packet and all same-packet death prevention before deciding whether a link remains for its repeat save.

The subject retains its decisions and an ordinary form attack. Losing hands/speech may restrict particular abilities, but the transformation does not impose whole-Action denial. A willing temporary creature-origin recipient with action-capable expressed anatomy can reject Polymorph, Mass or shaping True with its Action on its original regular turn. This permission remains while suppressed: a creature-origin object form temporarily expressing its root creature anatomy can reject then. Unsuppressed object anatomy is actionless and cannot reject; object-origin identities gain no player-style rejection right. Changing one's mind does not create hostile repeat saves. Shapechange uses ordinary concentration release and cannot invoke its internal switch while suppressed.

Mass makes independent saves for1–10 targets using preselected R4 profiles. For each target, O is the footprint remaining on a successful save and T is the footprint on failure/waiver. Before paying, every pair must support O/O, O/T, T/O and T/T without illegal overlap; each individual footprint must also fit terrain/other bodies. A target's own O/T may overlap. Apply successful changes simultaneously. Ending/replacing one target link leaves other links intact. There is no ongoing range tether.

## Endings, switching, suppression and geometry

Polymorph, Mass and Shapechange end at cast time+60seconds. True's stabilization checkpoint is the same absolute60seconds. Extra turns never extend these clocks. At a shared timestamp: finish an already-started event packet; process due hostile repeats; end successful saves; then expire temporary spells or stabilize surviving True links; then administrative cleanup. A successful final repeat prevents permanence.

Actual0HP, death or external Incapacitated after every same-packet replacement ends temporary spell anatomy, including both creature→creature and creature→object during True shaping. A legal “remain at1” keeps the form. Reversion never heals, clears Wounds, restores temporary HP or rerolls damage. Permanent True does not end merely at0/death; later dispel returns a still-dead/damaged original body and cannot recreate missing matter. Structural0 destroys an object-origin manifestation and releases its slot.

Shapechange's internal switch costs a Bonus Action, requires a different legal profile and space, and occurs at most once on each later original regular turn. It cannot occur on the casting turn, including a cast on an extra turn, and never occurs on an extra turn. It pays no new RP, makes no spellcast/Refrain event, resets no resources, and grants no free attack. Losing unsupported flight invokes ordinary falling.

A spell may successfully replace a Druid form, ending actual form-dependent effects without refunds. A Druid cannot Shapeshift while any spell-transformation record is active, including suppressed or permanent records. Temporary replacement requires at least the existing rank. Permanent True requires another successful True or an exact named exception. Same-profile new casts remain legal paid casts. These precedence checks apply to an old record that survives commitment; your own concentration record already ends when the new concentration cast commits.

Antimagic suppresses every transformation without ending its record. The root anatomy is expressed, concentration remains required where applicable, and the original clock continues. Temporary spells may expire while suppressed. True may stabilize while suppressed if concentration remains valid, then resume its permanent anatomy later. Suppression never releases a companion slot or creates a second hidden form. A suppressed record still follows the same replacement precedence.

Mandatory reversion uses the **same spatial anchor**. If root anatomy cannot fit, report `placementConflict` to canonical geometry. No automatic teleport through walls, free relocation or invented crushing damage occurs. Until resolved, overlap cannot establish legal movement/targeting through a barrier. **Open whole-game dependency:** the general mandatory-reversion geometry conflict procedure. The helper exposes this boundary rather than claiming that geometry subsystem is complete.

## True Polymorph object modes

True allows creature→creature, willing creature→object, eligible object→creature, and eligible object→object. Only one object/body is produced. Object input must be a discrete nonmagical, unattended, uncarried, unworn, unattuned Large-or-smaller object with canonical current/max structural HP. Artifacts, active magical devices, terrain/building structures, corpses/significant remains and undefined-durability objects are ineligible.

Those fresh-object admission checks apply to introducing an ordinary outside object. An already-active True Polymorph object anatomy can be replaced by another legal True Polymorph without pretending it is an unattended nonmagical outside object. A creature-origin person in object anatomy retains agency: creature-profile replacement permits a willing waiver or requires a CON save if unwilling; object-profile replacement requires willingness. Returning that person to creature anatomy preserves their original HP/Wounds/class/soul and creates no companion slot. Object-origin recasts retain all origin, value and slot constraints.

Object outputs are Tiny through Large, within one size category of the actual input, AC12, inert and nonmagical. Allowed templates: barrier/slab, ramp/wedge, open-container, static-furniture, simple-one-piece-tool. Static joined pieces and open hollow containers are allowed; actuated mechanisms, working hinges/latches/locks/keys, gears/clocks/traps, precision instruments, pressure vessels and documents/credentials are not. No output grants material resistance/immunity.

Require documented physical mass. Output mass cannot exceed the current input mass or earliest origin ceiling. Object-origin recoverable/sale value cannot exceed its earliest documented value; missing necessary mass/value makes that mode ineligible. Creature-origin object anatomy has no independent sale/salvage/harvest value. No mode produces food, medicine, ammunition, currency, gemstones, rare crafting material, valuables, consumable stock or magical properties. Chains never rebase the ceilings upward.

Creature→object retains the same character HP/Wounds/resources/history but supplies speed0, no Actions/Bonus Actions/Reactions, no speech/senses/hands. This is `actionlessObjectAnatomy`, **not** an automatic Incapacitated condition. A caster can therefore maintain their self-targeted shaping spell. Actual external Incapacitated still ends concentration/shaping normally. Permanent object anatomy has no voluntary rejection.

Object→creature uses a non-humanoid finite profile and exactly its existing structural current/max HP ledger. It has ordinary sight/hearing, saves equal to captured caster PB, ordinary unproficient checks+0, no special senses unless listed, no Wounds/death saves/Stable/dying state, soul, class/rest resources, reproduction, resurrection or XP/loot/corpse entitlement. At structural0, it is destroyed; dispel does not rebuild it. Temporary HP may protect it. Ordinary healing cannot repair it, even after later transformations; exact nonorganic repair is a separate source interface.

Creature-origin currently in object anatomy cannot newly receive effects requiring a creature/living creature/ally creature. Ordinary healing eligibility returns with creature anatomy if other requirements permit it. Already-attached effects retain their own exact lifetimes; a pulse needing fresh creature eligibility must recheck it. Transformation does not convert healing into object repair.

## Object companions

A successful object→creature application reserves one object-creature slot immediately, including shaping. It belongs to the original creating caster and stays occupied through stabilization, suppression, control changes and legal creature-profile replacements by other casters. Recasting the same body consumes no second slot and does not transfer control or sponsorship. A distinct second permanent creature cannot be created while the slot is occupied.

Release the slot only on actual ending/dispel to the original object, physical destruction or an allowed replacement into object anatomy. A later fresh object→creature casting after such an ending uses its new creating caster's slot. No free dismissal exists after stabilization. Existing companion transformations do not automatically change their owner/allegiance.

Use the current controller's **shared** companion Bonus Action command and one offensive-companion allowance,60-foot command range and actual perception, attached resolution, and uncommanded move+Dodge. No separate full damaging turn appears. Source-qualified exceptions remain exact. If an issued command becomes illegal, resources stay spent and the order does not execute. Supplied attacks still belong to the subject, with the original transformation caster's statistics.

operational.targets: One willing ally other than yourself, perceived within range and line of effect. Neither participant may already participate in another Warding Bond, as caster or protected ally.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. In initiative, expires at the caster's tenth future regular-start marker after application; retain that virtual marker through initiative changes, departure or death. Outside initiative, expires 60 seconds after application; entering initiative preserves that absolute deadline. An already-passed start never counts. Ends earlier when concentration ends. Also ends if either participant dies. Reaching 0 HP alone is not a separate ending condition; ordinary Incapacitated/concentration rules still apply.
operational.resolution: Automatic on legal casting. On each eligible positive incoming damage packet to the ally, apply the mandatory post-defense transfer described below; a rounded-zero transfer claims no transfer operation.
operational.effect: The ally gains +1 AC and +1 to saves, subject separately to the strongest applicable flat bonus. After the ally's defenses and legal prevention, before temporary HP, transfer floor(remaining damage / 2) to you and leave the remainder on the ally. Keep the damage type. Your transferred share skips a second mitigation/prevention stage and cannot transfer again; apply your temporary HP, HP, applicable life-state protections, Wounds and concentration consequences normally. The ally retains the hit, failed-save, critical and attached-rider identity; you were not hit and did not fail that save merely because damage transferred.
operational.scaling: None. The rank-2 duplicate grants no upgrade or extra effect.
operational.limitations: Use DAMAGE_SHARING_PLAYTEST.md: one transfer operation per original-recipient damage root, across all owners. A prior pre-mitigation split preempts this transfer; competing positive mandatory post-defense claims are chosen by the original target. The retained ally portion cannot subsequently be transferred again after this split. Complete the current packet's split and life consequences before concentration failure caused by that packet ends the bond; never undo a committed share. One Warding Bond per participating creature across all casters; casting cannot create chains or cycles. Initial range/line of effect are required, but no continuing distance or line-of-effect tether is imposed. This ordinary spell neither consumes nor increases the Paladin class redirection round ledger and grants none of its named healing/resource riders or proc permissions. Unrelated downstream triggers still require their own exact source authorization. Direct HP payments are not damage and cannot be transferred. Known/prepared access, class-level gates, legal components, line of effect, payment before resolution, concentration transitions, Dissonance, Refrain and class cadence follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: Action, 30 feet, concentration 1 minute, +1 AC/saves and half-damage sharing; M/F uses focus. NEW: willing ally, conserved mandatory post-defense split, rounding, participation and life endpoints, no continued tether and ordinary-spell/class-engine separation. completeCounterparts.name: Counterspell

operational.activation: Reaction — when another creature you can perceive within range and line of effect begins casting a spell, after its casting costs and cadence are committed but before its effect resolves
operational.targets: One pending spell cast by the triggering creature. The spell needs an actual recorded rank; the Director may know that rank without revealing it to you.
operational.duration: Instantaneous
operational.resolution: make a spellcasting-ability check using the actual ability for the class through which you cast Counterspell, adding PB once, against DC 10 + twice the triggering spell's actual rank (rank 0 contributes 0). Use CORE_RESOLUTION_PLAYTEST.md's fixed-DC task degrees and natural shifts: at least DC+10 Critical Success, at least DC Success, at most DC-10 Critical Failure, otherwise Failure; natural 20 improves one degree and natural 1 worsens one. Collapse both upper degrees to success and both lower degrees to failure; invent no additional critical effect. This is not a spell attack or saving throw.
operational.effect: Success negates the selected pending spell after its costs were committed; failure lets it continue. Every interruptible cast first commits its RP/material/other costs, components, concentration transition, Dissonance/Refrain and exact beginning/casting hooks once, then opens the interruption window. A surviving cast later resolves its effect and outcome-dependent hooks. Negation gives no refund, no successful-effect trigger and no restoration of old concentration. Counterspell is itself a spell and can be countered. Resolve nested counters last-in, first-out; if a counter is negated, the earlier pending spell resumes without paying or casting again. Resuming a parent never rewrites the later nested cast's Refrain/Dissonance history.
operational.scaling: None. No automatic success against lower ranks and no generic upcast.
operational.limitations: One attempt per creature against a particular pending cast, shared across ordinary, Wizard, Mage and other same-named Counterspell sources. An exact source that expressly grants an additional Counterspell attempt against the same pending cast overrides this default; merely granting another Reaction does not. After a failed attempt another eligible creature may react; once negated, the spell supplies no further interruption trigger. All reactions need their own legal remaining resource, components, range and current source permissions. Attempting does not reveal spell identity/rank; never treat an unassigned rank as 0 or estimate it from RP. Ready opens its cast-interruption window at preparation, not release. Countering is not whole-Action/turn hard denial and does not spend that ledger. Ordinary Counterspell requires ordinary repertoire/class access and rank-3 cost; Wizard/Mage same-named class cards keep their own separate acquisition, printed costs, ranks, recharge and text. Apply SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md for actual class access and repertoire, costs before resolution, components, concentration, Dissonance/Refrain and exact source cadence. No automatic scaling or generic upcast.
operational.designNotes: PRESERVED: both Abjuration/Universal rank-3 placements, Reaction, 60 feet, V/S/F and instantaneous interruption. NEW: actual casting ability+PB against DC 10+2*rank, one attempt per pending cast, hidden-rank handling and nested timing. REVIEWED SOURCE CORRECTION: the earlier binary-check proposal is superseded by the existing Core fixed-DC task rule, with natural shifts and collapsed success/failure outcomes. Exact source permission may override the shared attempt limit; another Reaction alone cannot.

operational.targets: Two distinct willing creatures with actual RP pools, each perceived within 60 feet and line of effect. You may be one participant. Each participant must be free of another active Resonance Conduit.
operational.duration: Concentration, up to 1 minute. Either participant may spend an Action to transfer a positive integer of existing RP to the other while both are on the same plane, within 60 feet of one another and have line of effect. At transfer start the recipient must accept; choose an amount no greater than donor currentRP or recipient currently missingRP. Commit the Action and immediately deduct that amount from the donor. At resolution credit the same amount, capped at recipient actual maximumRP; any newly excess amount is lost.
operational.effect: The two creatures retain separate RP pools and maxima. Deducted pendingRP is not spendable by either party and cannot be committed again; only a completed credit enters the recipient's pool. At resolution the link and recipient acceptance must still exist and same-plane/range/line-of-effect gates must still hold. If an exact interrupt or loss of these conditions prevents the transfer after commitment, its RP and Action are not refunded. Ordinary movement outside the transfer gate suspends permission without ending the link or pausing duration; returning restores only future permission. Either participant may voluntarily end the whole link without an Action, including before agreeing to a new conduit; ending one participant's link releases both, but never reverses completed or committed transfers. The caster can maintain only one conduit and each participant can belong to only one at a time.

Copies cannot duplicate transfers or create spendable RP. No daily limit is added; named recovery ledgers, Dissonance, Refrain, actions and clocks remain unchanged. Suppression prevents transfer while applicable without pausing the endpoint; it never refunds a committed transfer. Renewed consent alone cannot revive an ended application. A later legal casting may create a new Resonance Conduit normally, paying all costs and establishing a new application and endpoint. A successful replacement has its own endpoint; stale cleanup cannot end the new application. A countered cast creates no replacement, although its concentration transition has already occurred. Actual class access, rank, preparation, V/S/F components, casting costs, Dissonance/Refrain, class hooks, concentration transitions and counter windows follow SPELL_INTEGRATION_RULES.md. currentGoverningExcerpts.exactText:
# Spell integration rules — provisional v0.1

Use this document with the [shared class rules](CLASS_PLAYTEST_RULES.md), the class's own engine and the [spell packet](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md). This is a staged development layer, not an approved-book replacement or a live companion update.

## What owns each decision

| Decision | Source used for this packet |
|---|---|
| Spell identity, every school placement and per-class rank/access | Preserved `src/data/spells.js`; do not collapse different class ranks into one global rank. |
| Common RP prices and additional spell evidence | Core Systems Known Descent V2. Its spell blocks are retained with the catalog summaries. |
| Class identity, engine, spellbook/preparation and cadence exceptions | The current class playtest packet. |
| Generic Dissonance/Refrain, action limits and core conditions | Shared class playtest rules; source Core conditions remain unchanged. |
| Missing targeting, exact endpoints, concentration ambiguities and exploit limits | Explicitly provisional decisions on each spell card. |

The approved Core V2 source has 936 spell blocks. The companion catalog has 848 unique IDs with 936 school placements, but leaves four metadata fields unspecified. These are different views of the source, not evidence that all casting details were absent. Core's generic “Automatic or opposed as described” does not supply a concrete save or targeting rule.

Eleven possible renamed entries remain comparative evidence in the register. Harmonic Bulwark's catalog summary says 5 temporary HP per RP while the possible historical Mana Shield entry says 2; its [individual transformation and buffer review](TRANSFORMATION_SPELL_PLAYTEST.md) now supplies the operational decision. Both source variants remain preserved. Other unresolved aliases stay pending their own review; matching names never silently merge effects.

Resonance Kindle now has [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_CONJURATION_CANTRIP_EXACT_REVIEW.md): Action/Self/V/S, recover 1 RP only when this spell reaches resolution. Its one character-wide use is spent at legal cast start and refreshes only on a beneficial completed long rest. The comparative Mana Kindle block remains separately preserved; its broader wording does not trigger recovery from other cantrips and its historical range grants no remote recipient. The [Conjuration cantrip status](CONJURATION_CANTRIP_REVIEW_STATUS.json) records this bounded decision and the other eleven approved cards.

## Select a spell

1. Choose the class through which you are learning/casting it. Check that class's school access and minimum **class** level on the card.
2. Use that class's spell rank and Core V2 cost. A different eligible class may receive the same spell at a different rank and level.
3. Record it in your allowed known, prepared or spellbook choices. An eligible catalog entry is not an automatic grant. Wizard and Druid keep their explicit preparation systems; fallback counts apply only where the class has no more specific rule.

## Resolve a cast at the table

1. Verify the available Action/Bonus Action/Reaction, its exact trigger, components, targets, range and line of effect. No legal target means no activation or payment. A target in an area still needs the card's eligibility. Total cover blocks direct targeting unless expressly overridden.
2. Choose a spell from your actual repertoire. Determine its class-specific rank and RP cost: rank 0–9 costs **0/2/3/5/7/10/13/17/21/26**. Add explicitly printed extra costs; Resonance Shield adds 1 RP even when the caster receives it as a cantrip. Generic Overcast is excluded.
3. Read Dissonance **before** casting. Limit = max(4, 2 + PB + max(0, casting modifier)). At limit/limit+3/limit+6, ranked spells cost +1/+2/+3 RP. At limit+6 ordinary rank-1+ casting is blocked. Cantrips have no strain surcharge but still build Refrain. An expressly granted traumatic-casting exception pays the cost and its printed trauma; it grants neither rank nor repertoire access.
4. Commit the legal cast's RP, materials and other printed costs before any attack/save or interruption. Perform its components and establish concentration if required, ending incompatible prior concentration. An ordinary missed, saved-against or countered legal cast refunds nothing and never restores displaced concentration.
5. At this cast's beginning, apply ordinary Dissonance and Refrain once: 0 base for rank 0, 1 for ranks 1–5, 2 for ranks 6–9; consecutive same-named casts add Refrain +1/+2/+3, capped at +3. First cast or a different name adds +0. Apply the class's exact protected reduction, routing or vent and any hook whose printed trigger is beginning/casting. Weapon or idle turns do not reset the previous name/Refrain unless the class expressly says so. This chronological commitment occurs before the Counterspell window; a later Reaction cast updates its own history, and resuming the earlier cast does not update that history again.
6. Open legal cast-interruption Reactions, resolving nested counters last-in, first-out. A surviving cast then resolves its effect: spell attacks are d20 + PB + the actual casting ability modifier; save DC is 8 + PB + that modifier. Use the exact card's hit/failure/success results and ordinary damage/conditions. Outcome-dependent class hooks occur only at their printed timing and with the required actual result. No automatic cantrip scaling applies. A negated spell grants no success/hit/damage effect merely because its casting cost was paid.
7. Record concentration, exact expiration, per-rest use, summon and companion command obligations. A second spell cannot supply an ungranted Action, duplicate concentration or resource reset. A readied spell commits this casting sequence at preparation; release has no second cast, cost, cadence update or Counterspell window.

Countering requires an actual operational spell or class card, its repertoire/access and a legal remaining Reaction. ## Falling bridge — new provisional procedure

This is a newly authored table procedure agreed with the GPT notebook, **not recovered V6/Core V2 canon**. Focused searches of the current rulebook extract, Core V2 and mechanics/manual text found spell summaries but no operational falling clock or impact formula. Before promotion to canon, inspect the approved V6 environment/travel/hazard sections and archived environment tables. Preserve any older rule found and compare it explicitly.

When a creature loses support with no movement mode or effect keeping it aloft, it enters **Falling** immediately. Falling means unsupported; it grants no hovering, airborne walking or lateral movement. Track total distance descended during this fall and cumulative distance during its current uncontrolled portion, both initially zero.

**Timing:** If a fall begins during a regular initiative turn, set a fixed Fall Marker at the **end of that initiative slot in the following round**. Resolve the first Falling Step there, then one at the same marker each round. Reactions and extra turns use the enclosing regular initiative slot; an event between slots uses the most recently completed slot. Extra turns, extra Actions and initiative changes neither move nor multiply the marker. This gives every participant one normal turn opportunity before the first descent; inability to act still matters and no free rescue action is granted. A caster still needs legal targets within range when spending their Action.

Outside initiative, when timing matters, establish an order before descent and use a virtual slot immediately before its first regular slot as the initiating slot. The first step occurs when that virtual slot next recurs, after everyone has had one normal turn opportunity. When no rescue or other timing decision is possible, the Director can resolve the same descent and impact calculation directly. This is an explicit timing abstraction, not a model of physical acceleration.

If a fall begins after initiative has been established but before any regular initiative slot has yet completed, treat the virtual pre-round slot as the most recently completed slot for Fall Marker purposes.

**Ordinary descent:** At each step descend up to **300 feet**, stopping on a supporting surface. Add the distance to both trackers. On landing while uncontrolled, take **min(10, floor(uncontrolled distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning damage**. The uncontrolled distance includes earlier steps; never use only the final step's remainder.

**Feather Fall:** The spell retains its **Action** casting time and reduces descent to at most **60 feet per step**. When it takes effect, set uncontrolled distance to zero: the magic dissipates prior uncontrolled momentum in this abstraction. Keep total fall distance. If landing while it remains active, damage is **min(3, floor(total fall distance / 20))d6 bludgeoning**. This explicitly limits impact exposure without guaranteeing a harmless landing. When the spell ends aloft, reset uncontrolled distance to zero, then accumulate ordinary descent from that point at the existing marker; expiry grants no immediate extra step. Its one-minute maximum ends immediately before the caster's regular turn ten rounds after casting. If expiry and a step coincide, resolve expiry first. Earlier landing or cessation of Falling ends the spell on that target as printed.

Apply damage defenses only when their actual wording covers that damage. After damage, Falling ends; a creature suffering any positive falling damage lands **Prone** unless an explicit feature prevents it. Less than 20 relevant feet produces zero damage. Forced movement that removes support starts a fall but adds no separate fall damage. Regaining genuine support, secure support from a hold, or flight ends Falling without resolving an uncompleted impact; teleporting safely onto support likewise ends it. A later loss of support begins a new fall with new trackers and marker. Completed impact and damage cannot be undone by later casting.

| Scenario | Steps to land | Impact |
|---|---:|---:|
| Ordinary 10 feet | 1 | 0 |
| Ordinary 20 feet | 1 | 1d6 |
| Ordinary 300 feet | 1 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 310 feet | 2 | 10d6 |
| Ordinary 610 feet | 3 | 10d6 |
| Feather Fall active through a 310-foot fall | 6 | 3d6 |
| 120 feet slowed, spell ends aloft, then 190 feet uncontrolled | 3 | 9d6 |

The 300-foot ordinary step, impact formulas, momentum reset, marker and duration conventions are provisional inventions. The source supplies Feather Fall's Action, five targets and 60-foot slowed descent. Wider hazards, equipment catches, flight loss and environmental damage still need the combat/campaign pass.

**Alignment Suggestion:** calculate each new one-step shift with all prior same-spell overlays ignored, retaining independent actual alignment changes. Only changed defined axes receive fixed overlay values. A no-change result creates no replacement; the caster's already-required concentration transition still occurs and never resurrects an old application. A valid changed-axis application replaces the previous same-spell application; replaced concentration maintains no remaining effect. Ending exposes the then-current underlying alignment, not a historical snapshot. No conduct, belief or oathbreaking is compelled.

**Resonance Influence:** compute ordinary legal spell price first, including mandatory extras, Dissonance, eligible source reductions/waivers and each feature's own minimum. Then apply final plus/minus1, minimum0. A feature's minimum1 reduction step is not a universal final-price floor. Ease can offset one RP of the resulting total, including a mandatory Resonance Shield extra. A genuine RP-priced spell reduced/waived to0 still qualifies; Burden makes it1. In Mage Spell Sharing, the Mage's earlier sharing payment is unchanged, while the ally's later actual shared spell is independently priced: Ease0/Burden1. An ally unable to pay cannot commit, leaves Influence pending, and still uses the original limited sharing window. Nonspell techniques and charge-only spells without an RP-price interface do not qualify merely because they have costs. Qualifying class discounts require their actual class/spell eligibility; examples do not reclassify nonspell techniques. No runtime implementation or numerical balance is certified by this manuscript ruling.

## Rank-two Enchantment and shared control integration

Seven rank-two Enchantment identities have [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK2_EXACT_REVIEW.md) with no functional card repairs. Their [shared control integration](ENCHANTMENT_CONTROL_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md) is part of this provisional rules overlay and applies its specific arbitration interface to existing Command and Confusing Flash as well as Illusive Commands, Dire Charm and Crown of Madness. Their prior individual card texts remain unchanged.

The integration defines native ordinary Attack Actions and the explicit Confusing Flash single-attack exception; separately scoped Dire Charm components; chronological priority for conflicting instructions using the same ordinary budget; a shared six-second cycle for ongoing Dire Charm/Crown control outside initiative; and first-real-turn budget carry without replaying control orders. Ordinary real-turn start processing still occurs. One-shot commands keep their own timing while sharing actual remaining budgets.

Calm Emotions and Zone of Truth keep independent first-exposure save histories in fixed zones, with total-cover/outside suppression and return without rerolling. Calm Emotions suppresses actual Frightened effects while underlying clocks and saves continue. The five compared emotion-themed class cards acquire no new maintenance dependency. Zone of Truth preserves both actual class/rank/price modes without granting additional access or a truth-detection oracle. The [review status](ENCHANTMENT_RANK2_REVIEW_STATUS.json) retains open numerical balance, effect-runtime and broader social-control work.


## Rank-three Enchantment: companion control, source modes and task scope

Eight further identities have [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_EXACT_REVIEW.md) with no functional repairs. Their [rank-three integration supplement](ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_INTEGRATION_PLAYTEST.md) is part of this provisional overlay. It explicitly binds Dominate Beast and Suggestion to existing instruction arbitration, supplies the owner-attached Beast-companion bridge and prevents duplicate commands/turns. Hypnotic Pattern retains Enchantment60ft versus Illusion30ft casting range, and its initial self-concentration collapse uses only the reviewed spell-specific atomic batch.

Terrifying Gaze and both Slow modes use the reviewed ending-save transition without generating action budgets. Slow preserves Action/WIS Enchantment and Reaction/CON Transmutation as separate source packages; its selected trigger creature, distinct movement segments, future-Reaction restriction and prospective Action ceiling are explicit. Mental Chains uses the actual voluntary boundary and original anchor with separated-plane suppression, without universal involuntary-transport immunity. Suggestion reserves necessary hard control at establishment, including conditional future tasks, and never dynamically acquires a new hard component. The [review status](ENCHANTMENT_RANK3_REVIEW_STATUS.json) retains human balance, effect-runtime and broader-system work as open.


## Evocation cantrips: actual casts, delayed riders and source-specific attacks

Twelve cantrips have [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_EVOCATION_CANTRIP_EXACT_REVIEW.md) without functional repairs. Read the full cards in [the spell reference](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md); all fourteen source placements/Core blocks and actual class-access rows are retained. Their components remain V/S, with no added focus or automatic damage scaling.

Arcane Echo grants one genuine Bonus Action recast with the original actual class/school/rank-0 damaging-mode provenance, normal current eligibility/costs/hooks and chronological Refrain. Its arm and generated repeat keep separate finite records; a generated repeat never triggers another arm. Freezing Touch delays its Speed rider until the next regular target turn, with the expressly reviewed virtual-to-actual onset and original absolute cap. Flame Lash preserves the source conflict as a spell-local 30-foot melee attack. Shocking Grasp retains Reaction/30 feet and its prospective Reaction denial, without canceling a committed parent Action or stacked Reaction.

Dancing Lights has actual usable illumination for either generating school and bounded commanded movement. Chill Touch blocks broad current-HP gain, including direct recovery, while retaining independent non-HP effects and the existing resurrection life-transition exception. Its blocked natural20/Stable procedures use the existing healing-state rules. Soundburst and Thunderclap preserve distinct areas/riders; Thunderclap includes its caster. The object procedures never grant generic worn-item targeting. [Review status](EVOCATION_CANTRIP_REVIEW_STATUS.json) retains runtime, human balance and broader game integration as unfinished. Cosmology remains outside this mechanics batch.


## Rank-one Evocation attacks and maintained effects

Twelve rank-one Evocation identities have [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_EVOCATION_RANK1_EXACT_REVIEW.md), preserving thirteen placements/Core blocks and actual class access. Its card expressly applies ordinary Shield's named Magic Missile exception, with one targeting opportunity per recipient before that recipient's first missile damage. This does not alias Mage Arcane Missile. Arcane Shield Shatter requires an individually perceived rank-0/1 spell protective layer and a protected creature, with exact source-qualified eligibility. Its current Resonance Shield grant and whole Protective Sphere procedures prevent stripping unrelated temporary HP or inventing a hole in a boundary.

Witch Bolt's maintenance uses an ordinary Action to activate its existing effect. It is not another cast. Its pulse-use history survives initiative changes while preserving the Action for other uses when a pulse was already spent. Zephyr Strike grants no attack at casting; its first weapon-hit rider and continuing movement protection have separate consumption rules. Ignition Bolt and Ice Knife retain their short source ranges and captured impact positions; only attack damage dice critically double. Earth Tremor creates finite magical difficult terrain on one contiguous supporting surface. See [review status](EVOCATION_RANK1_REVIEW_STATUS.json) for the remaining runtime and human-balance questions.


## Rank-two Evocation areas and delayed damage

Eight rank-two Evocation identities have [exact manuscript approval](../../../../docs/audit/2026-10-08/full-game/GPT_EVOCATION_RANK2_EXACT_AND_DELIVERY_REVIEW.md). Their [complete cards](SPELL_PLAYTEST_STARTER.md) preserve five exact Core blocks and three separate possible historical-name blocks; matching metadata adoption does not merge identities or class access. Scorching Raystorm uses three independent attacks; line and burst spells keep their printed ranges. Shatter uses one fixed pre-damage snapshot and bounded structural sections. ## Reviewed ancestry spell access

The [ancestry/background integration](ANCESTRY_BACKGROUND_PLAYTEST.md) defines a separate explicit casting source for40 fixed grants and two Wizard-cantrip choices. These grants use their own total-level gates, ability, school/mode and recharge; they do not create ordinary class access, an RP pool or RC conversion. Charge-only casts retain actual components/actions/concentration/interruption and shared Dissonance/Refrain, have no RP-price interface, and remain blocked at their actual Limit+6 for ranked casting. The [seventeen dependency procedures](ANCESTRY_SPELL_SUPPLEMENT_PLAYTEST.md) comprise seven existing IDs promoted into this ordinary catalog and ten separate ancestry-grant-only additions.
